patch.value: A truncated list-all answer is consumed as if it were complete

readPmItems reads the SDK list (list-all alias) result's .items without consulting the result's completeness receipt (truncated / has_more / completeness.status / omission_receipt). Verified on this host against the 682-item workspace: pm 2026.8.14 returned 10 items with truncated=true, and a context pack built from ten items reported success while missing 98% of the workspace. 2026.8.15 fixes the default, but truncated can still go true under an output budget and completeness.status can go partial when items are unreadable — each must refuse loudly instead of producing a partial pack that reports success. Related: @unbrained/pm-cli resolves through floating ranges (^2026.8.7 dev, >=2026.8.7 peer), which is how the 2026.8.14 regression reached this package with no diff to review.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Wired all four refusal signals into readPmItems (the single list-all data path; the SDK list action is the list-all alias): truncated===true, has_more===true, completeness.status!==complete ('partial' and 'unchecked' both trip; a missing receipt also trips), omission_receipt.has_omissions===true. Each refusal is a CommandError naming the tripped signal and the count-vs-total figures; no partial list, no warn-and-continue. The list call now also passes noTruncate:true and strictRead:true so the engine itself refuses instead of degrading. Chose REFUSAL over a paging loop. No spawnSync exists on this path (in-process SDK action), so there is no spawn buffer to size; the completeness receipt is the over-run guard.

Revert-proof (removed only the assertListResultComplete(result) call, rebuilt, ran the new tests): all four refusal tests failed with 'AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected rejection'; happy-path and real-CLI baseline tests still passed. Fix restored; full suite 215/215.

Tests drive the refusal from a REAL pm list-all --json envelope captured from the CLI (temp 3-item workspace), one field mutated each, injected through the readPmItems list-action seam defaulting to the real SDK action. Exact-pin: devDependencies ^2026.8.7 -> 2026.8.15 and peerDependencies >=2026.8.7 -> 2026.8.15; node -p resolves 2026.8.15 after npm ci. Coverage 100/100/100 (lines/branches/functions) — thresholds unchanged.

author: claude-agent

value.author: claude-agent
value.text:
Review round 2 (CodeRabbit + Greptile on PR #63) — both findings adopted, and the Greptile finding turned out to understate the defect.

ADOPTED (CodeRabbit) — the list seam discarded its request argument, so nothing asserted what `readPmItems` actually asks the SDK for. The completeness receipt catches a truncated answer *after the fact*; `noTruncate: true` and `strictRead: true` are what stop the CLI from producing one at all. `seamFor` now captures the request and the happy-path test asserts the complete request object, so dropping either flag fails the suite instead of silently reverting to the read that returned 10 of 682 items. Verified non-vacuous: removing `noTruncate: true` from index.ts fails the test.

ADOPTED, with a larger root cause (Greptile P1) — Greptile reported that `manifest.json` declared exact compatibility with 2026.8.15 while the peer accepts newer, so the host would reject versions npm allows. The direction was right but the severity was understated. This package's manifest carried a `compatibility: { pm: "2026.8.15" }` block, and the pm host's version gate does not read that field at all — it reads top-level `pm_min_version`/`pm_max_version`. Confirmed empirically against the SDK's own `checkExtensionManifestCompatibility`: the manifest returned `compatible: true` for every host tested back to 2026.7.1, including 2026.8.14, whose truncated `list-all` is the exact defect this package's refusals exist to catch. So the floor was not too strict — it was never enforced. Replaced with `pm_min_version: "2026.8.15"`; the gate now refuses 2026.8.14 with `pm_min_version_unmet` and still accepts 2027.1.1.

ALSO FIXED — the lockfile still carried the pre-floor exact peer while package.json declares `>=2026.8.15`, which would fail the release workflow's `npm ci` synchronization check. Lockfile regenerated.

ALSO FIXED (found by applying the sibling finding across this repo) — CodeRabbit flagged in pm-beads that an `omission_receipt` mutation assumed the receipt exists while the baseline accepts it absent, making the mutation throw a TypeError outside `assert.rejects`. This file had the identical latent bug; corrected here too.

DURABLE FIX — two regression tests now bind the compatibility claim: one ties `manifest.json` `pm_min_version` to the package.json peer floor, the other runs the SDK's own host gate against the manifest bytes on disk so a floor moved back into a field the gate ignores fails loudly rather than shipping as an unenforced claim. Both verified non-vacuous by restoring the old `compatibility` block.

value.text:
Correction to the wording of this item's closure record (CodeRabbit, PR #63) — appended, not rewritten.

The closure entry and the round-2 comment both describe the change as exact-pinning `@unbrained/pm-cli`. That is accurate for only one of the three declarations, and the imprecision matters because these three are exactly what drifted apart in the first place:

- `devDependencies["@unbrained/pm-cli"]` is an EXACT pin: `2026.8.15`. It decides which CLI this package's own gates run against, so it must be reproducible, and a range is how the 2026.8.14 truncated-`list-all` build reached packages with no diff to review.
- `peerDependencies["@unbrained/pm-cli"]` is a LOWER-BOUND range: `>=2026.8.15`. It tells consumers which hosts this plugin works with. An exact peer pin would make every later CLI patch a peer conflict under strict peer resolution, converting a compatibility statement into a lockstep release dependency.
- `manifest.json` `pm_min_version` is a MINIMUM, not an exact compatibility version: `2026.8.15`. It is the floor the pm host enforces at load time, and it must equal the peer floor because they are the same claim to two different installers.

So the correct summary of this change is: **an exact dev pin, and a matching floor stated to both npm and the pm host** — not an exact pin in three places. The regression tests added in this PR assert exactly that shape (the peer must match `/^>=\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`, and `pm_min_version` must equal the peer floor with the `>=` stripped), so the code was already right; only the record's wording was loose.

No history file was edited. This correction is appended as a new event, per the append-only contract.
